"""
Large-scale image generation has progressed through advances in data scale, quality, rebalancing, and recaptioning. However, conventional pipelines typically optimize task-specific datasets independently. The main challenge lies not only in curating each task-specific corpus, but also in organizing heterogeneous supervision according to the dependencies among generative capabilities. We propose a \textbf{capability-driven data infrastructure} that unifies capability-specific supervision construction with capability-aligned curriculum scheduling. This infrastructure consists of three specialized yet interoperable data engines, each delivering complementary relational supervision for text-image grounding, inter-image transformation, and image-knowledge association. Caption experts further align text-to-image (T2I) and editing supervision across tasks and levels of granularity. A multi-stage curriculum jointly evolves task composition, visual concept distribution, data quality, and image resolution in accordance with the dependency order of capability acquisition. Capability-aware evaluation closes the loop through targeted retrieval, expert construction, and gap-aware resampling. At scale, this framework curates a 440M-image T2I corpus, 120M editing pairs, and over 27M image-entity pairs. Using this infrastructure, we train multimodal diffusion models from scratch at two scales, with 3B and 6B parameters, respectively. We conduct quantitative evaluation on CPI-Bench, as well as qualitative assessments across diverse text-to-image and editing scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate broad visual coverage, versatile rendering, and effective transfer across generative capabilities.
